title: Taiwan Semiconductor Stock (TSM) Looks Too Cheap for Its Growth Outlook
detail:
Taiwan Semiconductor Stock (TSM) Looks Too Cheap for Its Growth Outlook
TipRanks

TSM
NVDA
AMD
AMZN
AVGO
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) stock looks too cheap for its growth outlook. The leading semiconductor foundry has fallen with the wider artificial intelligence (AI) trade. Shares are down roughly 26% since hitting an early-October peak of $487, pulled down by a semiconductor sell-off triggered by leadership turmoil at Nvidia (NVDA) and fresh U.S. export curbs.

On the company's third-quarter earnings call in October, CEO C.C. Wei said, "demand for our leading-edge technologies continues to be extremely robust." The company's October 2026 revenue also grew 59.7% year-over-year.

While AI spending could disappoint, and China restrictions carry real consequences, TSMC's customers still need more advanced manufacturing capacity than it can supply. At about 15.38x next year's earnings, I think the sell-off offers an attractive entry point. I therefore rate TSM stock a Buy.

AI Fears Have Overshadowed TSMC's Position

AI fears have overshadowed TSMC's position, in my view. Investors are questioning whether hyperscalers will earn adequate returns on enormous infrastructure spending. Nvidia's leadership turmoil has intensified uncertainty around its China business. The announcement from Washington earlier this week adds tougher foundry-customer checks and restrictions targeting China's remote access to advanced AI computing.

Those developments can remove potential orders. Nvidia is a major customer, and a broader spending slowdown would affect TSMC. Its customer diversity doesn't protect it from an industry-wide retrenchment. Rather, it provides exposure across competing chip designs.

Nvidia could lose some accelerator share while AMD (AMD) gains it. Both companies rely on TSMC for advanced manufacturing. Google (GOOGL) and Amazon's (AMZN) custom accelerators provide other routes for AI spending to reach the foundry.

Broadcom's (AVGO) designs are another example. Its latest quarterly filing says TSMC produced roughly 95% of wafers supplied by its contract manufacturers during the first nine months. So changing winners among chip designers needn't mean fewer orders for TSMC. That distinction is central to my thesis. Customers can compete fiercely over AI profits while continuing to buy manufacturing services from the same supplier.

title: Pricey Walmart Stock Falls More Often, Not Harder
detail:
Pricey Walmart Stock Falls More Often, Not Harder
Trefis Team
Wed, November 18, 2026 at 12:55 PM MST 6 min read
WMT
COST
TGT
AMZN
KR
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Walmart reports its third quarter tomorrow, Thursday, Nov 19, before the market opens. Most previews will ask what its holiday outlook says about the shopper. This article asks a narrower question. Does Walmart stock fall harder on report day when it starts out expensive?

The short answer is no, not harder. But it has fallen more often when it starts at 40 times earnings or more. Across 31 reports since Feb 2019, the link between the starting price-to-earnings multiple and the report-day move is close to zero. The biggest fall, 11.4% in May 2022, came at 30.4 times earnings, in the middle of the range. Yet the last three reports all started above 40 times earnings, and the stock fell after each one.

That matters now. Walmart closed at $127.52 on Tuesday. That is 46.0 times its earnings over the past four quarters. Only three past reports started at a higher multiple.

How We Measured Each Report Day

The price-to-earnings multiple, or P/E, is the share price divided by a year of earnings per share. We used earnings per share under standard accounting rules, called GAAP, for the four quarters before each report. The report-day move runs from the close before the release to the close on report day. Walmart released all 31 reports before the market opened. Prices before the stock split on Feb 26, 2024 are divided by three.

Over the whole record, the stock fell on 16 report days and rose on 15. The average move in either direction was 3.9%. Up or down has been close to an even split.

Three Groups, Sorted By Starting Multiple

We sorted the 31 reports by starting P/E and cut them into three groups. The table shows how each group did.

August 2026 started at 40.1 times, so it falls in the middle group. The middle group had the deepest average fall, 6.2%. It includes the worst day, in May 2022. The most expensive group fell 3.8% on an average down day. By this cut, expensive starts did not produce bigger drops.

The difference shows up in the average move. The cheapest group gained 0.7% on an average report day. The most expensive group lost 1.0%. A split at 40 times earnings, which also takes in August 2026, points the same way. Reports at 40 times or more averaged a 1.7% loss. Reports below that line averaged a 0.7% gain. Above the line, the stock fell on 7 of 12 report days. Below it, the stock fell on 9 of 19.

That second cut also makes the falls look a little larger at high multiples. The average fall was 4.6% at 40 times or more and 3.7% below it. So the size of the falls depends on where you draw the line. The direction of the average move does not.

Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) drew a Buy rating from UBS as the firm assumed coverage with a lower $340 price target, and shares rose 0.89% to $260.17 in premarket trading at 8:59 a.m. ET on November 18. The previous target was $352, and shares had closed at $257.89 on November 17.

AMZN GF Value chart

UBS lowered its 2027 AWS revenue growth estimate to 43% from 48% and its 2027 AWS operating margin estimate to 40% from 45%, Yahoo Finance reported, while calling Amazon a defensive AI play because AWS works with any model and any chip. Amazon's own third-quarter results showed AWS sales up 39% to $46.0 billion with $17.8 billion of operating income, and total operating margin at a record 13.9%. The company guided fourth-quarter operating income to $28.5 billion to $33.5 billion and expects about $220 billion of 2026 capex.

AWS earned roughly a 38.7% margin last quarter, so the reduced 40% estimate for 2027 still implies modest expansion, not compression. GuruFocus gives Amazon a GF Score of 93/100, reflecting strong profitability, a solid balance sheet and healthy momentum, at about 21 times earnings. The $340 target sits about 31% above the premarket price. The next test is whether AWS growth holds near 40% as $220 billion of annual capex comes online.

title: Agility Robotics Opened at $11.26 and Dropped to $6. Here’s the Price Where I’d Buy the First Humanoid Robot Stock.

Agility Robotics Opened at $11.26 and Dropped to $6. Here’s the Price Where I’d Buy the First Humanoid Robot Stock.

Agility Robotics (NASDAQ:AGLT), a developer of humanoid robots for warehouses, logistics hubs, and manufacturing plants, went public through a merger with a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) on Nov. 5. Its stock opened at $11.26, but it now trades at about $6.60. Let's see why Agility fizzled out -- and what price would make it a compelling buy.

What does Agility Robotics do?

Agility's main product is Digit, a bipedal humanoid robot that can move heavy items while navigating aisles, ramps, and stairs on its own. Its top investors include Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN).

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Agility's Digit v5 robot. Image source: Agility Robotics.

Agility has already signed multi-year contracts with Toyota (NYSE:TM), GXO Logistics (NYSE:GXO), MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI), and Schaeffler, and its backlog has swelled to more than $300 million in committed orders for its newest robot, the Digit v5.

How fast is Agility Robotics growing?

Agility's backlog gives it plenty of room to grow, but it only generated $1.78 million in revenue in 2025 and $360,861 in revenue in the first nine months of 2026. It posted a net loss of $138.1 million in 2025 and an even wider net loss of $458.7 million in the first nine months of 2026.

Agility has only shipped a handful of its Cassie research robots to research institutions, and earlier versions of the Digit to a few commercial and industrial customers. For the full year, analysts expect it to generate only $846,200 in revenue with a net loss of $583.7 million.

That red ink made it tough to invest in Agility's market debut, especially as elevated interest rates and other macro headwinds drove investors away from riskier growth stocks. However, Agility claims it can deploy its first Digit v5 robots by the end of 2026, and scale its annual deployments to 800 units in 2027, 7,000 units in 2030, and 25,000 units in 2035. Its customers will need to pay recurring "robot as a service" (RaaS) subscription fees to keep them running.

Agility's $300 million backlog includes orders for 1,000 robots with bundled RaaS fees. If it successfully fulfills those orders, analysts expect its revenue to rise to $37.8 million in 2027 and $108.9 million in 2028. But with a market cap of $1.74 billion, it already trades at 16 times its 2028 revenue -- and it's expected to remain unprofitable for the foreseeable future.

title: Should You Buy Amazon Stock Before the Holiday Season?
detail:
Should You Buy Amazon Stock Before the Holiday Season?
Micah Zimmerman, The Motley Fool
Wed, November 18, 2026 at 11:05 AM MST 4 min read
AMZN
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The packages stacking up on porches over the next six weeks are the least interesting part of the holiday season for Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN). Selling more stuff in December is a given. What matters for the stock is how much of each sale Amazon gets to keep, and this year that answer looks unusually good.

Black Friday Week starts Nov. 19 and runs through Cyber Monday on Nov. 30, with deals up to 60% off and, for the first time, two deal drops on both Black Friday and Cyber Monday. Amazon is also hiring more than 300,000 seasonal, part-time, and full-time U.S. workers.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

So should you buy first? I think yes, though not for the reason most people expect.

Image source: Getty Images.

The holiday math has changed

For the fourth quarter, Amazon expects sales of $240 billion to $247 billion, up 12% to 16% from a year ago. Operating income, the profit from running the business, should land between $28.5 billion and $33.5 billion, up 14% to 34% from last year.

That gap is the story: Profit growing faster than sales means the store is getting more efficient. Last quarter, Amazon's operating margin hit 13.9%, its highest ever, and its North America segment's operating income jumped to $8.7 billion from $4.8 billion.

Advertising is the fuel. Every gift hunter, and every fan watching live sports with in-game shopping on Prime Video, is someone a brand will pay to reach. Amazon expects ad revenue to grow in the high teens this quarter, after a Prime Day timing shift held it to 12% last quarter. An ad doesn't need a truck or a warehouse worker, which is why I think it's the most profitable dollar in the building. Alexa for Shopping, Amazon's AI assistant, was used by more than 400 million customers over the past 12 months, and interactions rose 570%.

Don't buy it for a December pop

Shares slid after third-quarter results missed Wall Street's estimates as AI spending worried investors, per CNBC. They closed at $266.66 on Nov. 13, and the company is worth about $2.88 trillion. At the middle of its profit guidance, that's about 26 times a full year of operating income.

That's a reasonable price for one of the biggest retail stocks, which also owns the cloud computing leader, with Amazon Web Services growing 39% last quarter. It's also cheaper than plenty of AI stocks with far less to show.
